extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners building controllable headline-generation tools; newsroom technologists and editors interested in responsible headline optimization
extracted.subtask_description: Rewriting neutral news headlines with a large language model under inference-time control to increase reader engagement while avoiding clickbait and preserving semantic fidelity. The approach uses an engagement-attribute rubric, synthetic data, two auxiliary guide models, and FUDGE-style guided decoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information gap control
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute capturing withholding vs calibrated disclosure of facts in a headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Curiosity gap' — deliberate withholding of essential facts to compel a click by creating unresolved curiosity. Clickability Interpretation: 'Information gap calibration' — partial disclosure that invites interest while preserving the core factual claim. The rubric frames acceptable use as calibrated partial disclosure that preserves the core claim and unacceptable use as manufacturing unresolved curiosity by withholding essential facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which importance/impact/certainty is linguistically amplified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Exaggeration' — overstating importance, impact, or certainty beyond what is supported by the article. Clickability Interpretation: 'Proportional emphasis scaling' — adjusting linguistic intensity to match the true significance of the event. Guidance: scale emphasis to actual significance; avoid amplification beyond what the article supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of affective language to trigger fear, outrage, excitement, or concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Emotional trigger' — manipulative activation of fear, outrage, or excitement disproportionate to the facts. Clickability Interpretation: 'Affective salience framing' — highlighting emotionally relevant aspects implied by the content without inflation. Guidance: frame emotion only where implied by content and avoid manipulative inflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salience allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Which elements of the story are foregrounded and whether dramatic/marginal aspects are overemphasized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Sensationalism' — focusing on dramatic or marginal aspects at the expense of informational balance. Clickability Interpretation: 'Salience-oriented framing' — foregrounding the most newsworthy element while maintaining contextual integrity. Guidance: keep informational balance; avoid privileging marginal drama over contextually central facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural emphasis (Lists or Superlatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of lists, rankings, and superlatives to imply exceptionalism or order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Lists or superlatives' — use of absolute rankings or hyperbolic enumeration to imply exceptionalism. Clickability Interpretation: 'Structured highlighting' — bounded use of ordering or comparison to organize key information. Guidance: use lists/superlatives only to legitimately organize salient points and avoid hyperbole that implies false exceptionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referential clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which entities and referents are specified vs left vague.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Ambiguous references' — vague entities or pronouns that obscure meaning to provoke curiosity. Clickability Interpretation: 'Referential under-specification' — temporary abstraction that is resolved through reading without misleading. Guidance: temporary abstraction acceptable only when resolved by the article; avoid vague referents that mislead or force clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader addressing
rubrics_metrics.description: How directly the headline addresses or appeals to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Direct appeals' — imperative or coercive language explicitly urging the reader to click. Clickability Interpretation: 'Reader relevance cues' — implicit signaling of why the story matters to the reader. Guidance: prefer implicit relevance signals over coercive imperatives that pressure clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the headline leaves narratives unfinished or indicates continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Unfinished narratives' — artificial cliffhangers that omit essential outcomes. Clickability Interpretation: 'Narrative continuation cues' — indicating that further context follows while retaining essential information. Guidance: avoid cliffhangers that omit essential outcomes; use continuation cues that promise more context without hiding key facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Framing via associations or cross-domain linkages between concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Unexpected associations' — forced or misleading linkage between unrelated concepts. Clickability Interpretation: 'Cross-domain framing' — novel but factually grounded connections that increase interpretive interest. Guidance: ensure novel linkages are factually grounded and not misleading or forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogative form
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of questions as a headline device and whether they presuppose facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clickbait Interpretation: 'Provocative questions' — questions implying false premises or exaggerated stakes. Clickability Interpretation: 'Interrogative framing' — questions used to frame inquiry or uncertainty without presupposition. Guidance: avoid questions that embed false premises or mislead; use questions to frame genuine inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement-as-graded, multidimensional rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat engagement/clickbait not as a binary stylistic label but as a continuous, decomposable set of linguistic attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: model engagement as a continuous multidimensional space where clickbait arises from disproportionate amplification of otherwise legitimate mechanisms. Use attribute-level modeling (e.g., curiosity, specificity, framing) to selectively strengthen or attenuate mechanisms rather than binary classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve semantic faithfulness (content fidelity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrites must preserve the original headline's underlying factual content and core semantic meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: synthetic generation prompts and decoding constraints must explicitly instruct 'Do not add new facts.' Controlled rewriting should enhance engagement while maintaining semantic fidelity; clickbait control (negative guidance) is used to avoid semantic distortion and misleading phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic dataset construction protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for creating paired neutral and clickbait variants for supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: start from curated neutral headlines (e.g., Reuters subset), treat them as neutral baselines, and generate one clickbait variant per source by activating up to three clickbait-oriented engagement mechanisms via attributed prompting. Each sample includes headline text, a binary clickbait label, and a sparse binary engagement-attribute vector indicating activated attributes. Ensure generated variants exaggerate only selected dimensions and preserve factual content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit tactic activation per generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Constraint on how many engagement mechanisms are amplified when generating a clickbait variant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: the prompt allows activation of up to three clickbait-oriented engagement mechanisms per generation to produce controlled, interpretable stylistic amplification and to create a dataset spanning 0–3 active tactics (neutral to increasingly amplified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefix-level supervision and terminal token convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Train and operate scoring/guidance models on token-level prefixes as well as full headlines; mark full headlines explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: decompose each headline into all token-level prefixes; append a terminal period token to the full headline while leaving prefixes unmarked so models can distinguish completed headlines from intermediate prefixes. This enables guidance models to provide signals during incremental decoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length-aware weighted loss for prefix training
rubrics_metrics.description: Weight training examples by prefix length to reduce noise from very short prefixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: down-weight loss contributions from very short prefixes relative to longer prefixes and complete headlines so models focus on informative contexts while remaining robust to partial inputs. Apply this strategy to both the clickbait scorer and the engagement attribute model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clickbait scoring model as negative guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A prefix-operating binary clickbait scorer that outputs a probability used to penalize candidate continuations during decoding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: implement by fine-tuning a BERT encoder with a binary classification head on prefix data; during decoding evaluate scorer on candidate extended prefixes and apply a penalty term -λ_neg * S_cb(x1:t⊕y) to token log-probabilities. Use scorer as a soft constraint (reduces probability of continuations that increase clickbait likelihood) rather than hard rejection. Because very short prefixes are unreliable, use length-aware loss during training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement attribute model as positive guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-label attribute predictor that provides fine-grained positive control signals for desired engagement mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: implement by fine-tuning a BERT encoder with a multi-class, multi-label head where each attribute is an independent prediction dimension. Train on prefixes and full headlines with length-aware weighting. During decoding obtain per-attribute normalized scores S_k(x1:t⊕y) and compute S_pos = Σ ω_k S_k where ω_k ∈ {−1,0,1} indicates encourage/ignore/suppress. Use λ_pos * S_pos as a positive bias in token selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: FUDGE-based combined guidance objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined scoring formula to reweight LLM token probabilities with positive and negative guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/formula: log p(y|x1:t) ∝ log p_LLM(y|x1:t) + λ_pos S_pos(x1:t⊕y) − λ_neg S_cb(x1:t⊕y). By adjusting λ_pos ≥ 0 and λ_neg ≥ 0 the system trades off engagement enhancement against editorial restraint. Use incremental evaluation of auxiliary models on candidate continuations to reweight token probabilities under a principled Bayesian factorization (FUDGE paradigm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent data leakage via source-level splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset splitting protocol to ensure synthetic variants of the same source headline do not cross train/validation/test boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: split the curated source headlines at the source-headline level (e.g., 80% train/validation, 20% test) before synthetic generation and prefix expansion so that variants of the same source headline remain within a single split. This prevents leakage across prefixes and ensures valid evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and interpretability practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics and analyses to validate scorer and attribute model behavior and generation quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: evaluate the clickbait scorer (e.g., AUROC) on held-out synthetic test set and report per-attribute detection reliability (bar plots) and confusion matrices to reveal structured confusions among related tactics. Use qualitative tables comparing rewrites with and without clickbait control (varying λ_pos, λ_neg) to demonstrate effect on sensationalism and semantic fidelity. Recommend human judgments and real-world engagement metrics for future calibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt template constraint: 'Do not add new facts.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit prompt-level rule when generating synthetic clickbait variants to avoid fabricating facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance/Examples: prompts used to generate clickbait variants explicitly instruct the LLM to 'Deliberately withhold essential details' for curiosity tactic or to 'Overstate' for exaggeration, but always include 'Do not add new facts.' Table 2 examples show how a fixed prompt template with only the activated tactic changed yields controlled outputs (e.g., 'Rewrite the headline using the Curiosity Gap tactic. Deliberately withhold essential details... Do not add new facts.').
